summary: The founding moment of every multi-tenant app: a fresh signup has no group, needs to create the org AND their own membership atomically - but the group key is (correctly) stripped from client bodies, so plain CRUD can't express it. Declare groups.bootstrap and the framework provides POST /api/_groups/create.
example_app_yaml:
groups:
  table: company_members
  key: company_id
  user_field: email
  role_field: member_role          # optional - see tenant_roles below
  bootstrap:
    org_table: companies
    founding_role: company_admin   # written to role_field on the founding membership
identifier_rule: groups.table, key, user_field, role_field and bootstrap.org_table are spliced into the membership SQL as table/column names, so each must be a PLAIN identifier (letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit) naming a real table or column. A non-identifier value is refused at push / benmore check and at reload, not silently applied. The same rule holds for encrypted.yaml and the inline encrypted: table and column names, retention.yaml table/column, and a workflow's table/field in workflows.yaml.
endpoint: POST /api/_groups/create  body: org-table columns (e.g. {name: 'Acme Co'}) → 200 {status:'created', group_id, org:{...}, founding_role}. Auth required. 409 if the caller already has a group. One transaction: org insert + founding membership insert; the new group attaches to the live session immediately so the very next request is tenant-scoped.
behavior_notes: Org-table body fields are validated against the schema with the same protections as auto-CRUD (protected and computed columns stripped, user_id auto-injected when the org table has it, a workflow state column starts in its initial state, a submitted foreign key must name a row the founder can read - 422 otherwise - and constraint errors are generic outside dev mode).

The org table's DECLARED write mode applies to the founder: `companies: { write: admin }` or `write: role:sales` means only those callers may bootstrap an org. Not applied: no declaration (or only the global `default:`), `group` (a founder has no group yet) and `off` (the usual way to make bootstrap the only door). A `founding_role` named `admin` is a tenant role, not a global admin (see api({at:'rbac'})).

The org insert runs the same gates as an auto-CRUD create on the org table: `:validate` rules, validators.yaml cross-field rules and before_insert hooks (an aborting hook refuses the bootstrap with 422 and nothing is written). A scoped token needs write scope on both the org table and the membership table (403 otherwise). The one-group check is repeated inside the transaction, so concurrent or stale-session requests cannot found a second tenant.

Both inserts emit what an auto-CRUD insert emits: hooks.yaml on_insert hooks and on_insert event flows on the org table AND the membership table, with the row plus the session context (`{{user_group_id}}` is already the new tenant), webhook subscriptions for each table, and a realtime insert event for each. So a per-member provisioning hook or flow on the membership table runs for the founder too. The membership row is built from session and config only (no body field reaches it), and before_insert hooks run on the org table only. Both audit rows (`action: insert`) are written inside the bootstrap transaction with the row's id and every value written, the founding role included; if an audit row cannot be stored, nothing commits (500 `audit write failed`, or 507 when storage is full).

Switching between tenants a user already belongs to: POST /api/_switch_group {group_id} (live membership required; admins may switch anywhere). A JSON client (a JSON body or `Accept: application/json`, as bm.api sends) gets 200 {status:'switched', group_id} and refusals as {error}; a browser form post keeps the 303 redirect to the Referer.

Without bootstrap config, inserting into a group-keyed table with no group returns a GUIDED 422 (the tenant-key NOT NULL error explains the strip + points here) instead of the raw SQLite constraint error.

Joining an EXISTING org is membership management, not bootstrap - insert the membership row via an invite flow / admin action (see membership_management); the session lazy-resolves its group on the next request.

Reading the current tenant from the frontend: GET /api/_auth/profile (bm.auth.me()) carries `group_id` in a groups: app - the caller's effective tenant id as a string (an admin's act-as tenant while stepped in), null before they join or found one. That is the onboarding check (`if (!me.group_id) showCreateOrg()`); it names only the caller's own tenant. The SDK drops its cached profile after a POST /api/_groups/create or /api/_switch_group sent through bm.api, so the next bm.auth.me() has the new id.
